DeliHelper#GitHub repository: AlexSmed/DeliHelper
Project Description#DeliHelper is an application designed to make everyday work easier for restaurant and deli employees. It provides a central place to store recipes, important information, and routines, helping employees find the information they need to carry out their tasks.
The application also integrates Google’s Gemini AI to check products for potential allergens, helping employees identify allergy-related concerns.
Technologies Used#Language: Java Web framework: Javalin Persistence: JPA / Hibernate Database: PostgreSQL Build tool: Maven Authentication: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) Architecture#The application uses a layered architecture to separate responsibilities:
Controller layer: Handles REST endpoints and incoming requests. Service layer: Contains the application’s business logic. Repository layer: Handles database access. Features#Centralized storage for recipes and important information. Access to routines and procedures for restaurant and deli employees. Product allergy checks using Gemini AI. Persistent data storage using PostgreSQL. JWT-based authentication. My Contribution#I developed DeliHelper independently, taking responsibility for the application’s implementation and its different layers.
One challenge was deciding how to handle allergy information when integrating Gemini. I considered whether to check against a comprehensive list of allergies or use a more focused list. Including every possible allergy could make the results harder to read, so deciding how to present relevant information clearly was an important design consideration.
I was also absent during some lessons covering security and deployment because I was ill. I caught up by studying the assigned material independently and completing the related work at home.
What I Learned#Through this project, I gained practical experience with Java backend development, REST APIs, database persistence, and layered application architecture. I learned how to separate controllers, business logic, and database access to make an application easier to maintain.
I also gained experience with authentication using JWTs and integrating an AI service into an application. Working on the allergy-checking feature taught me to think critically about how information is selected and presented to users, particularly when that information could affect food safety.
Developing the application independently also helped me improve my problem-solving skills and ability to learn new concepts outside the classroom.
